name: England
summary: England property purchase checks: residential SDLT, residence tests and local conveyancing.

rules.title: Residential purchase tax
rules.text: SDLT applies here. A qualifying non-resident residential transaction carries a surcharge of two percentage points; reliefs and exceptions exist. Additional-property rules require a separate assessment.

rules.title: Citizenship is not the SDLT residence test
rules.text: HMRC uses transaction-specific residence tests. A British passport, UK visa or ordinary tax-residence classification does not settle this test.

buyers.sa: South African nationals should obtain a local conveyancing and SDLT assessment, plus a South African outward-funding assessment where relevant.

rules.text: The authority says to apply for registration within three months of acquisition. Establish whether the transaction is real property or a housing-cooperative interest, which follows a different process.

sources.label: Swedish mapping and land-registration authority — ownership

buyers.uk: Ask local counsel to determine UK-national eligibility for this property and ownership structure. The formalities below do not establish an exemption from foreign-buyer rules.
buyers.eu: Identify the specific EU nationality and residence position. Confirm any special-land, local-use or permit conditions before committing.
buyers.sa: Ask local counsel to determine South African-national eligibility. Separately confirm the outward-funding route if you are resident in South Africa for exchange-control purposes.

gap: Identity and real-property registration requirements reviewed. Agricultural acquisition permissions, cooperative membership and nationality-specific eligibility require separate assessment.
local: Ask the appointed local practitioner to check the exact municipality, parcel, permitted use, tenancy position and any agricultural, coastal, heritage or security restrictions.

name: Switzerland
summary: Switzerland property purchase checks: Lex Koller and cantonal approval.

rules.title: Foreign non-resident acquisitions
rules.text: Lex Koller restricts acquisition by persons abroad. The canton determines whether authorisation is needed and whether a statutory ground permits it; an application is not a guarantee of approval.

rules.title: Ownership does not confer residence
rules.text: The Federal Office of Justice expressly separates buying property from the right to reside in Switzerland.

sources.label: Swiss Federal Office of Justice — foreign non-resident property acquisition

buyers.uk: Ask the competent canton to classify your nationality, actual residence, permit status and intended use under Lex Koller.
buyers.eu: EU nationality alone does not clear a non-resident purchase. Confirm Swiss residence status, use and any authorisation requirement with the canton.
buyers.sa: Obtain a cantonal Lex Koller assessment before committing; do not assume a holiday-home or main-home route is available.

gap: This entry covers the sourced checkpoints below, not a complete title, planning, tax or nationality-specific legal opinion.
local: Identify the canton and municipality. Holiday-home quotas, residence/use conditions and local second-home rules need individual checks.

name: Norway
summary: Norway property purchase checks: deed registration and municipal concession rules.

rules.title: Deed and concession position
rules.text: Kartverket’s deed guidance requires the concession position to be resolved with the municipality, through permission or the relevant declaration of exemption where applicable, before registration.

buyers.uk: Nationality alone does not settle concession, residence-duty or registration requirements. Obtain a municipality-specific assessment.
buyers.eu: EU/EEA status does not remove the need to resolve concession and land-use requirements.
buyers.sa: Confirm the municipal concession position and identity/registration arrangements before transferring the price.

gap: This entry covers the sourced checkpoints below, not a complete title, planning, tax or nationality-specific legal opinion.
local: Check concession, agricultural land, residence duty and holiday-home use with the exact municipality. Cooperative interests require their own documents.

name: Monaco
summary: Monaco property purchase checks: property regime, notarial review and Rocher pre-emption.

rules.title: New Rocher legislation
rules.text: Law 1.598 of 16 October 2026 creates a defined protected perimeter in Monaco-Ville and provides state pre-emption and prior-declaration requirements for covered disposals. Its scope is not all Monaco property.

buyers.uk: Ask local counsel to determine UK-national eligibility for this property and ownership structure. The formalities below do not establish an exemption from foreign-buyer rules.
buyers.eu: Identify the specific EU nationality and residence position. Confirm any special-land, local-use or permit conditions before committing.
buyers.sa: Ask local counsel to determine South African-national eligibility. Separately confirm the outward-funding route if you are resident in South Africa for exchange-control purposes.

gap: The new Rocher law is a specific checkpoint, not a complete Monaco acquisition code. Foreign-buyer eligibility, protected-sector occupation/letting rules, other pre-emption regimes and transitional provisions require a Monaco notary’s current assessment.
local: Identify the exact building and property regime. Obtain written confirmation of any protected-sector, occupation, declaration or state pre-emption conditions and their satisfaction before completion.

name: South Africa
summary: South Africa property purchase checks: tax treatment, conveyancing and cross-border funds.

rules.title: Transfer Duty or VAT
rules.text: SARS explains Transfer Duty on property acquisitions and its administration through the conveyancing process. Determine whether the transaction is subject to VAT instead and obtain a current calculation.

rules.title: Non-resident seller withholding
rules.text: A buyer can have a withholding obligation when purchasing South African immovable property from a non-resident seller for more than R2 million. Obtain conveyancer advice before paying the full price.

buyers.uk: Ask a South African conveyancer to confirm eligibility for the exact asset, tax registration where applicable, incoming-funds evidence and any lending conditions.
buyers.eu: Ask a South African conveyancer to confirm eligibility, purchase-tax treatment and incoming-funds documentation. A property purchase does not grant immigration residence.
buyers.sa: Confirm ordinary conveyancing and tax requirements. If funds or ownership cross a border, establish your exchange-control residence and the correct banking route.

gap: Tax checkpoints reviewed. This entry does not certify that every foreign individual may acquire every land category, or establish a universal non-resident mortgage limit.
local: Identify the province and municipality. The nine provinces are Eastern Cape, Free State, Gauteng, KwaZulu-Natal, Limpopo, Mpumalanga, North West, Northern Cape and Western Cape. Check municipal zoning, building approvals, land use, sectional-title/community obligations and any special-land restrictions.
